# Known-red ledger for the split-root contract rig (#593).
#
# Format: <pytest node id> <owning issue>
#
# These cases fail when the product root and the instance root are genuinely
# different directories, and pass in a fused checkout.  They are deselected
# from the split-root suite run so the job can gate the rest, and then run
# individually by the "Assert every known-red case is still red" step: if one
# starts passing, that step fails and the entry must be deleted in the same PR
# that fixed it.  Nothing here is a skip.  Do not add an entry without an
# owning issue, and do not add one to silence a failure you have not diagnosed.
#
# Both current entries are the same class, and the class is an open question
# rather than a known-bad test.  Each caller sets AGENTS_HOME explicitly to
# select an instance root, and an ambient AGENT_FABRIC_INSTANCE_ROOT outranks
# it, so the explicit selection is silently ignored.  Today that is invisible:
# the two roots are the same directory, no ambient instance root is exported,
# and the tests pass by coincidence.  After #565 an exported instance root is
# the normal state, so this precedence decides whether a user who sets
# AGENTS_HOME gets the root they asked for.
#
# The tests encode one answer (explicit AGENTS_HOME wins); the runtime
# implements another (ambient AGENT_FABRIC_INSTANCE_ROOT wins).  #563 owns
# choosing, and must then fix whichever side is wrong.  This rig deliberately
# does not assume which - it only makes the disagreement fail out loud instead
# of resolving itself by coincidence.

tests/test_instance_installation.py::test_the_standalone_cli_refuses_a_relative_environment_instance_root #563
tests/test_provenant_cli.py::test_split_root_preserves_instance_root_for_mcp_child #563
